summary: Build practical third-party due diligence, screening, ownership, and remediation skills. Review the course and strengthen your controls.
lede: Third-party due diligence helps procurement, compliance, grants, and legal professionals assess external organizations before and during a relationship. The training focuses on making documented onboarding and monitoring decisions for suppliers, agents, consultants, and implementing partners. Participants practise assessing risk, verifying beneficial ownership, documenting screening decisions, and planning monitoring and remediation.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who assess, approve, contract, monitor, audit, or remediate third-party relationships across procurement and donor-funded operations. It suits experienced practitioners and adjacent control functions who need a common due diligence workflow without requiring legal or investigative specialization.
prerequisites: You should have working exposure to procurement, supplier management, grants administration, compliance, legal review, internal audit, or contract administration. No legal qualification, investigation certification, or programming experience is required. Familiarity with your organization’s supplier or partner onboarding process will help you apply the exercises. Bring anonymized process information only, with no confidential personal or third-party data.
